rule: Minimize usability risk
rationale: Prefer clear, familiar, legible choices when a design detail could be misunderstood or missed.
agent_check: Flag ambiguity, low legibility, unfamiliar affordances, or precision-dependent interaction.
exceptions: Novelty is acceptable when it solves a real problem and is validated.

rule: Require a rationale for meaningful design details
rationale: A design decision should be explainable by user, task, accessibility, hierarchy, consistency, or business value rather than taste alone.
agent_check: Ask what user problem each prominent style or interaction solves.
exceptions: Purely decorative details can exist if they do not harm usability.

rule: Minimize total interaction cost
rationale: Optimize the combined physical and mental effort needed to complete the task.
agent_check: Count tapping, scrolling, searching, reading, typing, remembering, waiting, and precision movement.
exceptions: Extra interaction can be worthwhile when it reduces errors or cognitive load.

rule: Minimize cognitive load
rationale: Reduce unnecessary decisions, information, and interpretation so attention stays on the task.
agent_check: Look for clutter, unclear grouping, inconsistency, excessive choice, and hidden relationships.
exceptions: Complex domains may require complexity, but it should be structured and staged.

rule: Use a design system
rationale: Constrained tokens and reusable components reduce decision overhead and improve consistency.
agent_check: Check whether repeated styles and components use shared rules.
exceptions: Small prototypes can start lighter, but reusable patterns should still emerge.

rule: Design for accessibility
rationale: Interfaces should be usable by the widest practical range of users and situations.
agent_check: Review contrast, color dependence, target size, focus, labels, semantics, and magnification.
exceptions: Use current authoritative accessibility standards even when newer than the book.

rule: Prefer common design patterns
rationale: Familiar controls reduce learning, cognitive load, and usability risk.
agent_check: Identify bespoke interactions that duplicate a familiar platform pattern.
exceptions: Depart when the conventional pattern performs poorly for the actual task and evidence supports a better solution.

rule: Prioritize high-impact use cases
rationale: Spend effort on the small set of tasks and problems that drive most user value or complaints.
agent_check: Rank flows by frequency, value, and severity before polishing edge cases.
exceptions: High-risk edge cases can outrank frequency.

rule: Account for implementation and testing cost
rationale: Prefer simple, familiar solutions when custom complexity does not create proportional user value.
agent_check: Ask whether bespoke UI increases design, engineering, QA, or training cost without measurable benefit.
exceptions: Strategic differentiation can justify cost.

rule: Keep similar things visually and behaviorally consistent
rationale: Consistency reduces relearning and error probability.
agent_check: Compare repeated components, vocabulary, layouts, and interactions for inconsistent behavior.
exceptions: Intentional variants are acceptable when the semantic difference is real and explicit.

rule: Show interaction states clearly
rationale: Interactive elements need visible feedback so users understand availability and response.
agent_check: Check default, focus, pressed/active, hover where applicable, selected, loading, and disabled states.
exceptions: Touch-only interfaces may not need hover, but still need equivalent state feedback.

rule: Remove nonessential information
rationale: Every extra item competes for attention.
agent_check: Ask whether each visible item is needed for the current task or decision.
exceptions: Retain legally, operationally, or safety-critical information.

rule: Remove nonessential styling
rationale: Decorative differences can create false hierarchy and distraction.
agent_check: Flag shadows, colors, borders, badges, and containers without semantic or structural purpose.
exceptions: Brand expression is valid when it does not compete with task clarity.

rule: Underline links when needed for recognition
rationale: Link styling should remain recognizable and not depend on color alone.
agent_check: Check whether inline links can be distinguished from body text.
exceptions: Navigation items and obvious UI link contexts may not need underlines.

rule: Use progressive disclosure
rationale: Reveal secondary information or controls only when they become relevant.
agent_check: Find advanced, optional, or rare content shown before it is needed.
exceptions: Do not hide critical information or prerequisites.

rule: Do not confuse minimalism with simplicity
rationale: Removing visible information can make a task harder even if the screen looks cleaner.
agent_check: Check whether aesthetic reduction hides meaning, state, or action.
exceptions: Minimal visual expression is fine when task clarity remains intact.

rule: Keep important content visible or clearly discoverable
rationale: Critical information should not depend on users guessing where it is hidden.
agent_check: Identify high-value content behind unclear icons, menus, hover, or deep navigation.
exceptions: Secondary detail can be disclosed progressively with clear triggers.

rule: Design from the constrained screen first
rationale: Small-screen constraints force early prioritization and reduce accidental complexity.
agent_check: Check whether the core task works on the narrowest target viewport.
exceptions: Desktop-first may be appropriate for desktop-only dense workflows.

rule: Reduce choice to speed decisions
rationale: Decision effort grows as option count and complexity rise.
agent_check: Remove irrelevant options, group choices, stage them, or provide informed recommendations.
exceptions: Experts may need dense choice when speed comes from familiarity.

rule: Maintain sufficient contrast
rationale: Low contrast reduces legibility and control discoverability.
agent_check: Check text, icons, borders, states, and focus indicators against current accessibility criteria.
exceptions: Decorative elements without meaning are exempt.

rule: Never rely on color alone for meaning
rationale: Users with color-vision differences must still understand state and meaning.
agent_check: Require text, icon, shape, pattern, position, or other redundant cue.
exceptions: Color can reinforce an already clear signal.

rule: Use semantic system colors for status
rationale: Consistent status colors improve recognition and reuse.
agent_check: Check that success, warning, error, info, and neutral states have defined semantic roles.
exceptions: Brand constraints may alter exact hues, but semantics should remain distinct.

rule: Use color to support visual hierarchy
rationale: Color prominence should correspond to interaction or information importance.
agent_check: Flag strong color on low-priority decorative elements.
exceptions: Campaign or editorial surfaces can use broader color when hierarchy stays clear.

rule: Establish structure before adding color
rationale: A layout should work through spacing, type, and contrast before decorative color is relied upon.
agent_check: Mentally or visually desaturate the design and check whether hierarchy survives.
exceptions: Some data visualizations fundamentally encode categories with color, but still need redundant cues where required.

rule: Use subtle tints instead of harsh neutral extremes when useful
rationale: Slightly tinted neutrals can feel cohesive and reduce visual harshness.
agent_check: Check whether neutral tones fit the brand and preserve contrast.
exceptions: Pure black/white can be correct for specific brands and high-contrast needs.

rule: Keep brand color strategy simple
rationale: A dominant brand accent is easier to govern consistently than many competing brand colors.
agent_check: Check whether multiple accents create unclear interaction semantics.
exceptions: Mature brands may require a broader palette.

rule: Use brand accent consistently for important interactions
rationale: Repeated accent use can teach users what is interactive.
agent_check: Check whether the accent has a stable semantic role.
exceptions: Do not make every interactive element equally prominent.

rule: Define a small semantic color palette with usage rules
rationale: Named roles reduce inconsistency and speed decisions.
agent_check: Require tokens such as text, border, surface, interactive, success, warning, error.
exceptions: Data visualization may need additional categorical scales.

rule: Use a predictable color model for controlled variation
rationale: Systematic color adjustment is easier to maintain than arbitrary hex choices.
agent_check: Check whether tonal variants are generated intentionally.
exceptions: Any color model is acceptable if rules are explicit and accessible.

rule: Limit unnecessary tonal variations
rationale: Too many near-duplicate colors create inconsistency without user value.
agent_check: Identify token variants with no distinct semantic role.
exceptions: Complex visualization systems can require more.

rule: Design dark mode as its own accessible palette
rationale: Dark interfaces need deliberate contrast and elevation choices, not simple inversion.
agent_check: Review text, surfaces, borders, shadows, and semantic colors independently.
exceptions: Not applicable when dark mode is not supported.

rule: Use tonal contrast and shadow to communicate depth
rationale: Depth can clarify overlays, raised surfaces, and stacking order.
agent_check: Check whether elevation has a consistent semantic meaning.
exceptions: Flat layouts are fine when hierarchy remains clear.

rule: Use transparency deliberately
rationale: Transparent layers can adapt to different backgrounds while preserving state relationships.
agent_check: Check contrast across every background the element can appear on.
exceptions: Use solid colors when transparency makes contrast unpredictable.

rule: Tokenize transparent colors
rationale: Reusable overlays and alpha tokens prevent arbitrary state styling.
agent_check: Check whether overlay/state opacity values are standardized.
exceptions: Not necessary in very small systems.

rule: Use consistent overlays for interaction states
rationale: A systematic state treatment makes components feel predictable.
agent_check: Compare hover/press/selected overlays across components.
exceptions: Platform-specific state treatments can override.

rule: Name colors by semantic purpose
rationale: Semantic naming survives rebranding and helps agents/developers apply colors correctly.
agent_check: Prefer names like text-muted or border-strong over blue-300 when usage matters.
exceptions: Scale names can coexist with semantic aliases.

rule: Harmonize imagery with the interface palette carefully
rationale: Image treatment can improve cohesion when it does not distort meaning or content.
agent_check: Check whether temperature/tint supports the surrounding palette without reducing authenticity.
exceptions: Product, evidence, medical, or documentary imagery should not be misleadingly altered.

rule: Group related elements
rationale: Proximity, containers, similarity, and alignment communicate relationships.
agent_check: Check whether spacing and containers match semantic grouping.
exceptions: Dense expert tools may use compact grouping but still need clear boundaries.

rule: Create a clear visual hierarchy
rationale: Prominence should match importance and expected sequence.
agent_check: Rank what is seen first, second, third and compare with task priority.
exceptions: Intentionally equal elements can share prominence.

rule: Use a squint/desaturation test for hierarchy
rationale: If the main structure disappears when detail is blurred, hierarchy may rely on fragile cues.
agent_check: Review the screen at reduced detail or zoom.
exceptions: Data-dense interfaces may require finer-grained review too.

rule: Use depth only when it clarifies hierarchy
rationale: Elevation should indicate stacking, focus, or separation rather than decoration.
agent_check: Flag shadows/elevation without a structural role.
exceptions: Brand-led visuals may use stylistic depth if it stays subordinate.

rule: Reason explicitly about margin, border, padding, and content
rationale: Clear box-model reasoning prevents inconsistent geometry and hit areas.
agent_check: Inspect component outer spacing versus internal spacing and borders.
exceptions: Native platforms may abstract implementation details but the spatial logic still applies.

rule: Design at logical 1x units
rationale: Logical units improve consistency across display densities.
agent_check: Ensure spacing and target sizes use platform logical units rather than physical pixels.
exceptions: Follow the target platform unit system.

rule: Use a predefined spacing scale
rationale: A small scale improves rhythm and implementation consistency.
agent_check: Flag arbitrary one-off gaps unless justified.
exceptions: Optical adjustments can occasionally deviate.

rule: Use spacing to encode relationship strength
rationale: Items inside a group should generally be closer than separate groups.
agent_check: Compare intra-group and inter-group spacing.
exceptions: Intentional alignment or containers can supplement proximity.

rule: Use enough whitespace to reveal structure
rationale: Breathing room helps grouping, scanning, and focus.
agent_check: Identify crowded areas where unrelated items visually merge.
exceptions: Operational dashboards may need higher density but still require structured spacing.

rule: Use a consistent grid for large layouts
rationale: A stable grid improves alignment and predictability.
agent_check: Check major columns and content edges for consistent alignment.
exceptions: Mobile layouts often use simpler column systems.

rule: Align text for easy scanning
rationale: Consistent text edges reduce visual search.
agent_check: Check long text and lists for unnecessary centered/right alignment.
exceptions: Language direction and specialized numeric tables can require different alignment.

rule: Limit competing alignments
rationale: Too many alignment axes make a layout feel disorganized and harder to scan.
agent_check: Identify avoidable jagged or conflicting edges.
exceptions: Complex dashboards can use multiple grids when clearly structured.

rule: Keep related actions near the content they affect
rationale: Shorter movement and stronger association reduce mistakes and search effort.
agent_check: Check edit/delete/filter actions for distance from their target.
exceptions: Global actions can remain in stable global toolbars.

rule: Make layouts resilient to content variation
rationale: Interfaces should survive long labels, missing data, large text, small screens, and variable content.
agent_check: Test wrapping, overflow, empty states, dynamic type, and localization expansion.
exceptions: Fixed-format kiosk or signage contexts may have narrower constraints.

rule: Compose photos intentionally
rationale: Cropping should preserve subject focus and leave usable space for UI.
agent_check: Check focal point, crop behavior, and text-safe areas across breakpoints.
exceptions: Product imagery may require centered technical composition.

rule: Keep the primary interface typeface simple and legible
rationale: A reliable sans-serif base reduces complexity and supports UI legibility.
agent_check: Check whether multiple body/UI families add value or inconsistency.
exceptions: Brand/editorial products can justify other highly legible families.

rule: Use a second display typeface only for purposeful expression
rationale: A contrasting heading face can add emotion without fragmenting the whole system.
agent_check: Check whether the second face is limited and readable.
exceptions: Skip it for highly utilitarian products or when localization coverage is weak.

rule: Limit unnecessary font weights
rationale: A small weight set produces clearer hierarchy and fewer near-duplicate styles.
agent_check: Find semibold/medium/light variants that do not represent meaningful hierarchy.
exceptions: Dense design systems may need an extra weight if validated.

rule: Use a defined type scale
rationale: A type scale creates repeatable hierarchy instead of arbitrary sizes.
agent_check: Map each text role to a token and flag one-off sizes.
exceptions: Optical display sizes can occasionally deviate.

rule: Use comfortable body size for long reading
rationale: Long text needs enough size to avoid fatigue.
agent_check: Check reading contexts separately from compact labels and table cells.
exceptions: Dense data labels can be smaller when not used for sustained reading.

rule: Use generous line height for long body text
rationale: Adequate leading improves tracking from one line to the next.
agent_check: Check prose blocks for cramped lines.
exceptions: Compact labels, buttons, and large headings use different ratios.

rule: Reduce relative line height as type size increases
rationale: Large display text usually needs tighter leading to maintain visual cohesion.
agent_check: Review headings for excessive vertical gaps.
exceptions: Multiline accessibility or script needs can require more space.

rule: Keep prose line length within a readable range
rationale: Very long lines make it harder to find the next line and sustain reading.
agent_check: Constrain long-form text columns.
exceptions: Tables, code, and data views follow different rules.

rule: Prefer left alignment for long left-to-right prose
rationale: A stable left edge improves scanning in LTR languages.
agent_check: Flag centered paragraphs and long centered lists.
exceptions: Use right alignment for RTL languages and specialized data where appropriate.

rule: Tighten letter spacing carefully for large display text
rationale: Large type can appear too loose at default tracking.
agent_check: Check display headings optically rather than applying extreme tracking.
exceptions: Do not harm scripts or fonts whose spacing is already optimized.

rule: Protect text legibility over images
rationale: Image detail and changing luminance can make overlay text unreadable.
agent_check: Check all responsive crops and use scrims, placement, or separate surfaces when needed.
exceptions: Decorative text that is nonessential still should remain reasonably legible.

rule: Avoid weak text contrast and unnecessarily harsh extremes
rationale: Very light gray text can fail legibility, while nuanced dark neutrals can improve comfort when contrast remains adequate.
agent_check: Check semantic text levels against accessibility criteria.
exceptions: Pure black can be correct for accessibility, brand, or print-like contexts.

rule: Keep UI copy concise
rationale: Shorter text reduces reading and search cost when meaning is preserved.
agent_check: Remove filler, repetition, and needless qualifiers.
exceptions: Legal, safety, or explanatory content may require detail.

rule: Use sentence case by default
rationale: Sentence case is familiar and easier to scan than pervasive title case or uppercase.
agent_check: Check labels, headings, buttons, and navigation for inconsistent casing.
exceptions: Brand names and established platform conventions can override.

rule: Use plain language
rationale: Simple vocabulary expands comprehension and reduces interpretation time.
agent_check: Replace jargon, slang, and unnecessary technical terms.
exceptions: Expert users can benefit from domain terminology when it is actually familiar and precise.

rule: Front-load important information
rationale: Users often scan only the beginning of labels and sentences.
agent_check: Move differentiating or critical words earlier.
exceptions: Narrative/editorial content may intentionally build context.

rule: Order content from most important to supporting detail
rationale: Priority-first structure helps users understand the gist quickly.
agent_check: Check whether critical outcome or instruction is buried.
exceptions: Narrative content can use other structures.

rule: Limit abbreviations and acronyms
rationale: Unfamiliar shorthand adds memory and comprehension cost.
agent_check: Expand or explain terms on first use.
exceptions: Well-known domain abbreviations may be more efficient for experts.

rule: Limit uppercase text
rationale: Large amounts of uppercase reduce word-shape recognition and can feel visually loud.
agent_check: Flag long uppercase labels or paragraphs.
exceptions: Short codes, acronyms, or intentional small metadata can use uppercase.

rule: Break long content into descriptive sections
rationale: Headings and compact lists make structure visible and reduce search cost.
agent_check: Identify walls of text and rewrite into scannable groups.
exceptions: Very short content does not need extra structure.

rule: Avoid redundant first-person possessives in labels
rationale: Labels like “My email” can add words without adding meaning.
agent_check: Remove unnecessary possessive terms when context already establishes ownership.
exceptions: Use possession when it disambiguates between people or entities.

rule: Use vocabulary consistently
rationale: Changing terms for the same concept forces users to infer equivalence.
agent_check: Create canonical terms for entities, statuses, and actions.
exceptions: Different terms are valid when concepts are genuinely different.

rule: Use numerals for numeric information in UI
rationale: Digits are compact and easy to scan in interfaces.
agent_check: Check counts, dates, quantities, and metrics.
exceptions: Editorial prose and locale conventions may differ.

rule: Avoid unnecessary terminal punctuation in short UI labels
rationale: Short labels and headings often scan more cleanly without periods.
agent_check: Remove punctuation from standalone labels when grammar does not require it.
exceptions: Complete sentences, errors, help text, and accessibility clarity may need punctuation.

rule: Keep repeated UI labels similar in length when practical
rationale: Large length disparities can destabilize repeated component layouts.
agent_check: Review repeated cards, tabs, and buttons for avoidable verbosity.
exceptions: Meaning and clarity outrank visual symmetry.

rule: Make link text describe the destination
rationale: Descriptive links support scanning and screen-reader navigation.
agent_check: Replace vague “click here” or “learn more” when destination is unclear out of context.
exceptions: Very local context can sometimes make short links clear.

rule: Write actionable error messages
rationale: Errors should state the problem and tell users how to recover.
agent_check: Check whether the message names the failed input/action and the next step.
exceptions: Security-sensitive contexts may need to avoid revealing exploit-relevant detail.

rule: Define primary, secondary, and tertiary action weights
rationale: A small action hierarchy makes importance predictable.
agent_check: Map every button variant to a semantic weight.
exceptions: Additional specialized variants can exist but should not blur hierarchy.

rule: Use one primary action when one action matters most
rationale: Competing primary buttons make the next step ambiguous.
agent_check: Count high-prominence actions in the same decision context.
exceptions: If actions are truly equal, use equal secondary prominence instead.

rule: Use secondary treatment for alternatives or equal actions
rationale: Secondary styling preserves options without competing with the main path.
agent_check: Check whether alternative actions are over-emphasized.
exceptions: Equal critical decisions can use equal treatment.

rule: Use tertiary treatment for low-priority utilities and many destructive actions
rationale: Low prominence prevents utilities or destructive actions from dominating the interface.
agent_check: Review utility and destructive actions for excessive visual weight.
exceptions: Destructive actions requiring urgent attention may need stronger warning treatment.

rule: Avoid unexplained disabled actions
rationale: A disabled control often fails to tell users what is wrong or how to proceed.
agent_check: Prefer validation/recovery messaging or explain prerequisites adjacent to the control.
exceptions: Disable when execution is genuinely impossible or unsafe and the reason is obvious/communicated.

rule: Place actions in a predictable scan order
rationale: Stable placement reduces search and magnifier travel.
agent_check: Use platform convention for button order and keep highest-priority action easy to find.
exceptions: Native platform conventions override a generic left/right rule.

rule: Use specific action-oriented button labels
rationale: Users should understand the consequence before activation.
agent_check: Prefer verb plus object where helpful and avoid vague labels.
exceptions: Short familiar labels such as Save can be sufficient in context.

rule: Provide generous target size and spacing
rationale: Larger separated targets reduce missed and accidental activations.
agent_check: Check target box, not just visual glyph size, against current platform guidance.
exceptions: Dense desktop controls can use different minimums if pointer-focused and still accessible.

rule: Balance icon and text visually
rationale: Icon and label should read as one control without awkward weight or spacing.
agent_check: Check icon size, baseline, gap, and visual weight.
exceptions: Icon-only controls need stronger familiarity and accessible names.

rule: Add deliberate friction to destructive actions
rationale: Irreversible/high-cost actions need protection from accidental activation.
agent_check: Use confirmation, undo, typed confirmation, delay, or separation proportional to consequence.
exceptions: Low-risk reversible actions may be better served by undo than confirmation.

rule: Prefer a single-column form flow
rationale: A straight downward path lowers scanning cost and missed-field risk.
agent_check: Flag multi-column arrangements that force zig-zag reading.
exceptions: Short related fields can share a row when their relationship is clear.

rule: Minimize the number of fields
rationale: Every field adds work, error opportunity, and implementation cost.
agent_check: Require a reason for each field and consider infer, default, defer, or remove.
exceptions: Compliance and operational requirements can justify additional fields.

rule: Mark optional fields clearly
rationale: Users should not guess which fields they can skip.
agent_check: Add explicit optional marker when a mix of field requirements exists.
exceptions: Very short familiar forms with all required fields can omit markers if validated.

rule: Prefer opt-in disclosure for nonessential inputs
rationale: Optional fields shown by default increase apparent workload and complexity.
agent_check: Ask whether a branch should be revealed only after the user chooses it.
exceptions: Show optional fields directly when most users need them or hiding would add more cost.

rule: Make required and optional status unambiguous
rationale: Requirement status should be clear without relying on skipped instructions.
agent_check: Review labels and screen-reader semantics.
exceptions: Single-question or universally-required short forms can simplify if context is obvious.

rule: Match field width to expected input when practical
rationale: Control size helps signal expected input length.
agent_check: Avoid full-width short code fields when a narrower field is clearer.
exceptions: Mobile layouts may use full width for touch ergonomics and consistency.

rule: Use conventional field affordances
rationale: Users should instantly recognize what is editable and how selection works.
agent_check: Flag stylized controls that lose familiar shapes, labels, or indicators.
exceptions: Custom visual styling is fine if core affordances remain recognizable.

rule: Place critical helper text before input
rationale: Users need constraints before acting, not after making an avoidable error.
agent_check: Move important format/rule guidance near and before the field in reading order.
exceptions: Noncritical supplementary help can appear after or on demand.

rule: Do not replace persistent labels with placeholders
rationale: Placeholder text disappears, can appear prefilled, and often has weak contrast.
agent_check: Require a persistent visible label for ordinary fields.
exceptions: Search boxes can use placeholder-like prompts if accessible labeling remains available.

rule: Keep labels close to their controls
rationale: Close proximity strengthens association and reduces eye movement.
agent_check: Compare label-to-field distance against field-to-field group spacing.
exceptions: Complex inline editors may use compact alternative labeling patterns if clear.

rule: Prefer visible radio choices for small option sets
rationale: Visible options are faster to compare and require fewer interactions than a dropdown.
agent_check: For roughly ten or fewer mutually exclusive options, compare radio versus dropdown cost.
exceptions: Use dropdown/select when space or density is a stronger constraint.

rule: Use autocomplete for long known-item lists
rationale: Search is faster than scrolling long lists when users know what they seek.
agent_check: Replace large flat selects for country, product, customer, etc. with searchable selectors.
exceptions: Browsing-oriented lists may need categorized exploration instead.

rule: Use steppers for small numeric adjustments
rationale: Plus/minus controls reduce interactions for small increments.
agent_check: Use for quantities and bounded small changes; allow direct entry when useful.
exceptions: Do not use steppers for large ranges or arbitrary precise numbers.

rule: Use checkbox for deferred binary commit and toggle for immediate effect
rationale: The control should communicate whether the change occurs now or on form submission.
agent_check: Check whether the interaction model matches consequence timing.
exceptions: Platform conventions can adjust presentation but not the semantic distinction.

rule: Phrase binary choices positively
rationale: Positive labels reduce double-negative interpretation errors.
agent_check: Read the selected state as “Yes, [label]” and check for clarity.
exceptions: Negative phrasing may be necessary when the domain concept itself is negative and unambiguous.

rule: Break long forms into a few meaningful steps
rationale: Chunking lets users focus on one group at a time and can reduce mistakes.
agent_check: Group related questions, show progress, allow back/edit, and review before commit when appropriate.
exceptions: Do not create one screen per field, which can increase interaction cost.

rule: Group related fields under headings
rationale: Visible sections reduce the apparent complexity of long forms.
agent_check: Add semantic headings when one page must contain multiple groups.
exceptions: Very short forms do not need extra headings.

rule: Make control boundaries discoverable with sufficient contrast
rationale: Users need to perceive input and selection boundaries reliably.
agent_check: Check borders, toggles, checkboxes, radios, and steppers against non-text contrast requirements.
exceptions: Borderless patterns can work only if another strong affordance clearly defines the control.

rule: Choose validation timing deliberately
rationale: Different inputs need different feedback timing; premature or late errors both create friction.
agent_check: Select submit, on-blur, live, or hybrid validation based on error cost and task.
exceptions: Complex async validation may require specialized states.
